title: The Clock
paragraphs: A mystery and suspense anthology introduced by the personified Clock, presenting compact stories of crime, irony, danger, and unexpected consequences.

U.S. ABC suspense anthology created by Lawrence Klee and framed by the personified Clock/Father Time. GRH preserves 55 U.S. archive objects using the Haendiges 1-82 sequence, numbered 2-80 with gaps [1, 28, 30, 39, 41, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 62, 63, 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 81, 82]. The later 1955-56 Grace Gibson Australian version is a separate production using purchased/adapted U.S. scripts.

GRH documents the program through ABC New York production (November 3, 1946 to February 26, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] and ABC Hollywood production (March 4, 1948 to May 23, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Charles Webster (performer on 51 recordings), Clark Andrews (director on 51 recordings), Gene Kirby (announcer on 51 recordings), Lawrence Klee (writer on 10 recordings and creator on 2 recordings), Bernard Green (composer on 3 recordings, music director on 3 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, and conductor on 1 recording), Basil Adlam (conductor on 2 recordings and music director on 2 recordings), and Joe DeSantis (performer on 4 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include time, fate and consequences, deception, hidden identity and manipulation, love, jealousy and relationship conflict, crime and wrongdoing, supernatural or uncanny threat, and money, greed and financial motive.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar suspense anthology boom, New York-to-Hollywood production migration, Sustaining network economics and cancellation, and Separate Australian adaptation.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (15 shared credited people), [[show|suspense|Suspense]] (12 shared credited people), [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (10 shared credited people), [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (9 shared credited people), and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (9 shared credited people).
